correctness.rationale: The continuant recurrence makes the determinant primitive linear in the final diagonal entry: the preceding irreducible continuant divides neither the new bridge nor the shorter minor. On the hypersurface the diagonal partials are diagonal cofactors; in corank one the rank-one symmetric adjugate has a nonzero diagonal entry, whereas in corank ≥2 all cofactors vanish. Deleting zero bridges splits the matrix into path blocks of nullity ≤1 by forward substitution, including singletons. Thus corank ≥2 is equivalent to a cut with singular determinants on both sides. The three component equations are a prime regular sequence (products of integral varieties over C on disjoint coordinate sets), yielding codimension three and degrees j(n−j). Distinctness follows from the stated witness with just the j-th bridge zero: the constant-diagonal-two, unit-bridge minor of length m has determinant m+1, so the two endpoint substitutions kill the side determinants and give C_j=j(n−j). Across the cut only a bridge transposition can contribute a nontrivial cross-block term in the determinant expansion; hence F=UV−b_j²C_j. On C_j≠0 some coordinate other than the three distinguished variables is nonzero for n≥3, giving a projective chart; U and V replace the endpoint diagonals with unit linear coefficients. Completing and rescaling the bridge by a square root of C_j gives uv−w² with 2n−5 free parameters and radical local Jacobian ideal (u,v,w). The total degree is the degree sum for distinct equidimensional reduced components; S₂ and regularity in codimension one imply normality. The all-size argument does not depend on the archived finite grid data. Neither special intersection germs nor a global radical Jacobian ideal is verified.

Its edge-cut prime complete intersection, product degree and transverse rank-three argument apply unchanged, and normality follows from the same codimensions. This is demonstrable coverage by the published argument, not a priority finding or reliance on its uncited 'established boundary case' label. The frozen direct continuant identity is a convenient alternative proof of the same local model, not a distinct surviving finding as stated.
